kinds.d: Fossil sea lily: calyx and arms on matrix, plates, or loose stem segments (columnals).

x.d: Crinoids such as Actinocrinites gibsoni from the Lower Mississippian Edwardsville Formation around Crawfordsville, Indiana.
Early Jurassic crinoid of the Posidonia Shale at Holzmaden, Germany; a pseudoplanktonic log-raft colonist reaching close to 30 m overall, the largest known crinoid.
x.dt: large slabs and stem plates · up to 20–26 m stems

x.d: Disarticulated stem segments so abundant they form rock called encrinite, used historically as beads (St Cuthbert's beads, Indian beads).
x.dt: Lower Carboniferous limestone near Clitheroe, England

kinds.d: Fossil echinoderm (sea urchin, starfish, blastoid; crinoids are their own kind).

x.d: Heart-shaped infaunal sea urchin of the Late Cretaceous to early Eocene, found in chalk across Europe, Africa, Antarctica and North America.
Cake urchin or sea biscuit, a sand-dollar relative from the Late Eocene with living members.
Extinct stalked echinoderm or 'sea bud' of the Ordovician to Permian, peaking in the Mississippian.

kinds.d: Fossil lamp shell (brachiopod), loose, pyritised or on matrix.

x.d: Carboniferous spiriferid brachiopod named by Sowerby in 1818, known from Great Britain and Canada.

kinds.d: Fossil clam, oyster, scallop or other bivalve shell, whole, opalised or on matrix.

x.d: Curved Jurassic oyster, called devil's toenail; folklore held that carrying one prevented rheumatism.

v.d: Best-documented European species, Hettangian to Sinemurian Lias
Large species of the late Pliensbachian of England

x.d: Cretaceous and Jurassic oyster cemented by a cupped left valve; Exogyra texana is from Texas.

kinds.d: Fossil snail shell (gastropod), whole, agatised or on matrix.

x.d: Agate packed with freshwater snail shells of Elimia tenera from the Eocene Green River Formation, Wyoming, first misnamed for the sea snail Turritella.

v.d: Laney Member, Green River Formation, Sweetwater County, Wyoming: best-preserved shells

kinds.d: Fossil coral, solitary or colonial, rough, polished or on matrix. A dead modern coral skeleton is under Coral skeleton.

x.d: Polished fossil rugose coral Hexagonaria percarinata, Devonian, found as glacial pebbles on Lake Michigan beaches; Michigan's state stone since 1965.
x.dt: six-sided pattern shows when wet or polished · 25 lb limit on state lands

x.d: Rugose coral with a horn-shaped skeleton and wrinkled wall, abundant from the Middle Ordovician to the Late Permian.
Tabulate coral with closely packed polygonal corallites, Late Ordovician to Late Permian, described by Lamarck in 1816.

kinds.d: Fossil bryozoan colony (moss animal), such as Archimedes screw or fenestrate lace, on or off matrix.

x.d: Carboniferous to Permian bryozoan whose mesh is wound round a corkscrew-shaped central axis, after Archimedes' screw.
x.dt: screw axis isolated or with lace

kinds.d: Fossil graptolite colony, usually on a shale slab.

x.d: Tuning-fork-shaped graptolite, as in Didymograptus murchisoni; used to date Ordovician rocks.
Classic shale localities for graptolites include Abereiddy Bay in Wales and Dob's Linn in Scotland.
x.dt: black films, sometimes pyritised in three dimensions

kinds.d: Fossil sponge, whole or sectioned, loose or on matrix.

x.d: Silica-spicule sponges, common as fossils; Pattersonia ulrichi is an Ordovician example from near Cincinnati, Ohio.

notes: Ventriculites, LeGrand crinoids and starfish fossils left out: no retrieved page confirmed them (LeGrand page covers only a quarry town). Crinoid is a new kind split from Echinoderm fossil. Archimedes localities (Indiana/Kentucky) not confirmed on the page, so omitted.
